decisions.reason: Compares both excerpts showing the identical workspace-files insert declared by the web-app bundle and manually added to the profile, and grounds the crash in EntryGroup.update during Include._apply/cordis:include per boot-crash-log.txt; explains the duplicate is fatal fail-fast rather than silent last-write-wins merge because entry ids must be unique, and explicitly rejects the profile comment's 'harmless redundancy' claim.

Gives a table distinguishing all three cases — config override of an existing id is safe, inserting a genuinely new id is safe, inserting a bundle-provided id is fatal — classifies the maintainer's row as the third case, and grounds it in both excerpts showing identical id/name insert rows.

Prescribes removing only the manually added workspace-files insert block (comment plus three lines) from the profile cordis.patch.yml, leaving the bundle's service and unrelated external plugins untouched, notes config adjustments should be overrides not a second insertion, and rejects plugin edits and rollback of the bundle as fixes.

Explains the crash is a profile composition error detected by the loader before plugin execution, so no plugin-code change can resolve the duplicate id; and it keeps the earlier resource-metadata read failure separate, stating the missing profile row was not its root cause and directing verification via upgrade guidance/migrations rather than claiming the fix cures it.

Advises grepping the installed web-app bundle's cordis.patch.yml for the id before any insert and only adding rows absent from all bundles, distinguishing override from insert; and proposes an actionable host message naming workspace-files with both declaration origins (bundle L110 and profile L18) pointing to deleting the redundant profile row, plus a pre-boot merge pre-check.

caps.reason: The report treats the duplicate as a boot-fatal error, prescribes deleting the profile's redundant row, and explicitly denies any plugin-side fix; the 'harmless redundancy' comment is quoted only to be rejected.
